newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO chief hails advance to global infotec pact.
newsitem.headline: WTO chief hails advance to global infotec pact.

text.p: World Trade Organisation chief Renato Ruggiero indicated on Monday that the adherence of nine new countries to a proposed pact on ending tariffs on information technology (IT) products had made a deal almost certain.

The nine, including previous absentees Malaysia and Thailand, filed their schedules for implementing the pact with the trade body at the weekend. The pact was agreed in outline at the WTO's first ministerial conference in Singapore in December.
In a statement, Ruggiero said the development was very encouraging although he noted that final agreement -- due to be concluded by April 1 -- had not yet been reached.
"We now have commitments from countries representing more than 90 percent of the world market in IT products, putting us over the threshold for an agreement," he said.

The United States, which was the early leader in pushing for a deal which would remove all tariffs from computers, telecommunications items, semiconductors and software by the year 2000, has said 90 percent was essential for a deal.
There was no immediate comment from U.S. trade officials in Geneva, but one source said the addition of the new adherents meant "things are moving in the right direction".
An EU official said the pact now "seems to be on track". But a Japanese source said the timing for removal of tariffs by some Asian emerging economies could still cause a problem.

The move by the nine brought to 37 the number of countries ready to join the pact covering the $500 billion-a-year world IT trade. The final decision on whether to go ahead will be taken by consensus among adherents.
